subject: hex-shell-process.test.js flakes ~1 in 12 and it is a deploy gate
description:
Observed 2026-09-03 at 101/103, with 11 consecutive clean runs around it. Chris first reported it; I narrowed a 900ms read against a 1000ms watchdog to 400ms, got three clean runs, and called it chased. Three runs is not evidence about a 1-in-12 event, and I should not have reported it as handled. The margin change was real and the flake is narrower, but it survives. Suspects are the two assertions in the pg5 watchdog block ('a FAILED chain does not clear a flag it never set', 'the third attempt is refused as still outstanding'), which race real timers against a 1000ms watchdog. DURABLE FIX: make those assertions wait on an observable state transition rather than sleeping for a duration, so they cannot lose a race. Do NOT add retry-until-green, which converts a real signal into noise. This matters because deploy.sh gate 3.7 runs this suite: an intermittent red either blocks a good deploy or trains an operator to re-run, and the second is worse than the first.
[2026-09-03 19:27] FIX SHIPPED, EVIDENCE RECORDED HONESTLY, TASK LEFT OPEN.

Fix (commit d36cf8e08): one waitForText helper polls for the expected output with a bound, and on timeout reads once more and returns whatever IS there, so a genuine failure reports real product output rather than a bare timeout. Swept for the SHAPE rather than the two assertions Chris named: 8 sleep-then-read sites exist, 4 were 'wait until X appears' and now poll, 4 wait for a duration so a background settle happens and correctly stay sleeps.

EVIDENCE: 15 consecutive clean runs against the committed fix (127/127 each).

WHY THAT IS NOT PROOF, and why this stays open: at the observed pre-fix rate of ~1-in-12, P(zero failures in 15 runs | nothing changed) is about 28 percent. So 15 clean is consistent with the fix working and does not establish it. Twice before I called this fixed on three clean runs, which was far weaker evidence than this and still wrong.

THE ARGUMENT THAT ACTUALLY CARRIES IT is structural, not statistical: a sleep asserts 'by now the thing has happened' and can lose a race; a poll asserts 'the thing happened' and waits up to a bound to find out, so there is no timing window left to fall into. The statistics corroborate; the mechanism is the reason.

TWO METHOD ERRORS OF MINE WORTH KEEPING: (1) my first stress run was invalid because I edited the suite WHILE it measured the suite, so early and late iterations tested different code; discarded rather than reported. (2) I piped the stress script through 'tail -25', which buffers, so there was no interim visibility during a 12-minute run; use tee next time.

TO CLOSE THIS: see it survive real deploys over time, or run a larger stress (40+ runs puts P(miss) under 3 percent). Do not close it on today's 15.
[2026-09-03 21:48] 40/40 clean, 0 failures, 127/127 assertions each run. Run window 16:10-17:43 (~94 min). Suite mtime 14:48 and _app/hex/index.html mtime 13:20 both precede the window, so the suite was not edited while it measured itself (that error invalidated the first attempt, which was discarded). Pre-registered bar: at the observed ~1-in-12 pre-fix rate, P(40 consecutive clean | bug still present) = 3.1%, so a clean sweep is real evidence. Fix under test: d36cf8e08, waitForText observes a state transition instead of sleeping against a 1000ms timer.
